meta.title: Recursion, one frame at a time
meta.subtitle: Intro CS · Lesson 7
meta.author: CS101

objectives.statement: Learners can explain what a base case is and why recursion needs one.
Learners can trace a recursive function by hand to its result.

slides.actionTitle: A function that calls itself — let's make that feel obvious.
body: Recursion, one frame at a time

slides.actionTitle: By the end, you can explain a base case and trace a recursive call.
body: Explain why recursion needs a base case
Trace a recursive function by hand

slides.actionTitle: First, the part that stops the loop: the base case.
The base case is the question that needs no further recursion.
Can you spot what goes wrong without a base case?
body: What does factorial(0) return, and why?
What happens if we delete the base case?

slides.actionTitle: You can name the stop — now the step that shrinks the problem.
The recursive case rebuilds the answer from a smaller one.
body: Each call moves toward the base case
Trust the smaller call to be correct

slides.actionTitle: Trace factorial(3) one frame at a time.
Now trace one yourself before we reveal it.
body: Where exactly does it hit the base case?

slides.actionTitle: Every recursive function needs both halves working together.
Recursion is just a base case plus a step toward it.
body: Base case stops; recursive case shrinks
Trace by trusting the smaller call
